thrust_tf.quote: Raptor 3 engines deliver increased thrust, with sea-level variants now producing 250 tf (551,000 lbf) up from 230 tf (507,000 lbf), while vacuum engines produce 275 tf (606,000 lbf) up from 258 tf (568,000 lbf).

mass_kg.quote: Mass of the Raptor sea-level engines has been reduced to 1,525 kg from 1,630 kg.

no_shrouds.quote: Sensors and controllers are now internally integrated and covered by engine thermal protection, eliminating the need for individual engine shrouds on both Starship and Super Heavy.

bell_matches_faa.source: photo_cmp and faa_plume: Raptor 3's exit is 768 px across, Raptor 1's 767 px. The bell's traced outline (z 0.25, 0.42, 0.59, 0.76, 0.93, 1.07 m: r 0.619, 0.580, 0.531, 0.475, 0.412, 0.353) lies within 1 cm of faa_plume's 32-to-6 degree bell (0.610, 0.578, 0.535, 0.480, 0.415, 0.360), and the narrowest point of the stack (r 0.18 outside, z 1.53-1.63) sits where faa_plume's 60.06 in puts the throat.

height_m.source: photo_cmp, scaled by Raptor 1's nozzle exit in the same photo (faa_plume's 51.226 in = 767 px, so 1.696 mm/px; all three engines stand side by side on identical pallets, camera level with their middles); estimated: exit (y 2128) to the top of the gimbal cap (y 395)
height_m.note: Raptor 1 in the same photo measures 3.12 m (exit at y 2130 to its top plate at y 290)

open_questions: Nozzle: faa_plume's 2019 nozzle, the only one published; photo_cmp shows Raptor 3's bell matching it (facts.bell_matches_faa). Raptor 3's own expansion ratio is not published.
Plumbing behind the engine (the far side from photo_cmp) is not in any photo found: the far half of the stack is built as round as the near half.
Depth (y) of the turbopump, ribbed duct and S-shaped pipe from photo_sn1, whose viewing angle is itself estimated.
Built as revealed (SN1, 2024). Flight engines (spacex_v3) carry thermal protection over the sensors and controllers; no clear photo of a flight Raptor 3 found.
Thrust: 250 tf (spacex_v3, 2026) is used; spacex_x_r3 (2024) gave 280 tf. Thrust doesn't change the model.
Not modelled: small wiring and sensors, the blue shipping lids. The "1" is SN1's serial: flight engines carry their own numbers.

decals.name: serial
decals.source: photo_cmp: the "1" at x 3065-3135, y 1551-1651 (centre z 0.894 m, 0.204 m right of the axis on the bell's 0.439 m radius there, so 27.7 deg round from the front). Its blocks, in stem widths (22 px): the foot overhangs the stem 0.8 on each side (foot x 3082-3135, stem 3095-3116 above it), the flag 0.68 to the left; flag and foot each 16 px of the 100 px height. Foot 53 px across, 0.10 m along the skin (over cos 27.7); 0.18 m tall along the bell's slope. Its slant in the photo is the bell narrowing upwards (about 11 px over its height), so it is drawn upright.
decals.note: Painted as one sheet on the bell kept only inside these blocks (shapes: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in the marking's box, y down from its top), drawn here from the proportions in photo_cmp, not traced; its edges are geometry, so they stay sharp.
